grammar_choice.en_template: Before the 1950s, tourism was very much an industry {{1:which/what}} was fragmented; hotels, transport operators, travel agents, and tour operators all {{2:tended/tend}} to work independently of each other.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 1950년대 이전에는 관광 산업이 매우 분절되어 있었다; 호텔, 운송 업체, 여행사, 그리고 투어 오퍼레이터 모두 서로 독립적으로 운영되는 경향이 있었다.
explain: 선행사 industry(사물)를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 which — what은 선행사 없이 쓰임.
과거 시제 서술 문맥 → tended(과거형).

grammar_choice.en_template: Hotels were largely in the business of {{1:selling/sell}} {{2:bed nights/nightly beds}}.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 호텔은 주로 숙박 판매 사업에 종사했다.
explain: be in the business of + 동명사 — selling.
업계 용어 'bed nights'(1박 숙박 단위) — 'nightly beds'는 비표준.

grammar_choice.en_template: Airlines and railways {{1:were/was}} in the business of {{2:selling/to sell}} seats.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 항공사와 철도는 좌석 판매 사업에 종사했다.
explain: 주어 Airlines and railways(복수) → were.
be in the business of + 동명사 → selling.

grammar_choice.en_template: Travel agents, of course, were selling travel and holidays, but in each case they tended to operate {{1:very much/so much}} as {{2:individual/individuate}} businesses.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 물론 여행사는 여행과 휴가를 판매하고 있었지만, 각 경우에 그들은 매우 개별 사업체로서 운영되는 경향이 있었다.
explain: '매우 ~로서'의 강조 부사 very much — so much는 이 구조에서 자연스럽지 않음.
'개별적인' 사업체 → individual(형용사) — individuate는 동사.

grammar_choice.en_template: From the mid-1950s onwards, particularly in the UK, the growth of tour operators began to {{1:change/changing}} the nature of the industry from essentially individual business activities to more {{2:integrated/integrating}} activities.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 1950년대 중반 이후, 특히 영국에서, 투어 오퍼레이터의 성장은 본질적으로 개별적인 사업 활동에서 보다 통합된 활동으로 산업의 성격을 바꾸기 시작했다.
explain: begin to + 동사원형 → to change.
'통합된 상태'를 수식하는 형용사 integrated — integrating(능동 현재분사)은 문맥 부적합.

grammar_choice.en_template: Hotels, for example, were beginning to {{1:see/seeing}} customers as {{2:wanting/to want}} a range of services rather than simply buying accommodation.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 예를 들어, 호텔들은 단순히 숙박을 구매하는 것보다 오히려 다양한 서비스를 원하는 고객들을 바라보기 시작했다.
explain: begin to + 동사원형 → to see.
see A as + 동명사(wanting) — 지각동사 see의 목적격보어.

grammar_choice.en_template: So hotels began to develop shopping arcades and later to offer secretarial centres to try {{1:to increase/increasing}} the spend of guests within the {{2:hotel complex/hotel's complex}}.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그래서 호텔들은 쇼핑 아케이드를 개발하고 나중에는 호텔 단지 내에서 투숙객의 지출을 늘리려 비서 센터를 제공하기 시작했다.
explain: try to + 동사원형(목적) → to increase.
'호텔 단지'는 복합명사 hotel complex — 소유격 hotel's complex는 비관용적.

grammar_choice.en_template: Transport operators, particularly in the airline business, {{1:saw/had seen}} the sale of transport services as {{2:being/to be}} integral to a much wider need.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 운송 업체들, 특히 항공업계에서는, 교통 서비스의 판매가 훨씬 더 광범위한 필요와 불가분의 관계에 있다고 보았다.
explain: 서술의 전반적인 과거 시제 흐름 → saw.
see A as + 동명사(being) — 전치사 as 뒤는 동명사.

grammar_choice.en_template: Airlines {{1:offered/were offered}} insurance and accommodation {{2:booking/booked}} for travellers.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 항공사들은 여행자들을 위한 보험 및 숙박 예약 서비스를 제공했다.
explain: 항공사가 서비스를 '제공한' 능동태 → offered.
accommodation booking(숙박 예약) — 명사구 수식 → 동명사 booking.

grammar_choice.en_template: So the tourism industry moved from {{1:being/to be}} essentially fragmented to {{2:being/be}} essentially integrated.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그래서 관광 산업은 본질적으로 분절된 상태에서 본질적으로 통합된 상태로 이동했다.
explain: from + 동명사(being) — 전치사 from 뒤에 동명사.
to + 동명사(being) — 전치사 to 뒤에 동명사(구조 병렬).

vocab_choice.en_template: Tourism was very much an industry which was {{1:fragmented/integrated}}; hotels, transport operators, travel agents, and tour operators all tended to work {{2:independently/collectively}} of each other.
vocab_choice.ko_full: 관광 산업이 매우 분절되어 있었다; 호텔, 운송 업체, 여행사, 투어 오퍼레이터 모두 서로 독립적으로 운영되는 경향이 있었다.
explain: 서로 협력이 없던 상태 → fragmented(분절된).
각자 따로 움직임 → independently(독립적으로).

vocab_choice.en_template: Hotels were largely in the business of selling {{1:bed nights/flight seats}}.
vocab_choice.ko_full: 호텔은 주로 숙박 판매 사업에 종사했다.

vocab_choice.en_template: Airlines and {{1:railways/hotels}} were in the business of selling {{2:seats/rooms}}.
vocab_choice.ko_full: 항공사와 철도는 좌석 판매 사업에 종사했다.

항공·철도의 상품 → seats(좌석).

vocab_choice.en_template: Travel agents were selling travel and holidays, but they tended to operate as {{1:individual/collective}} businesses.
vocab_choice.ko_full: 여행사는 여행과 휴가를 판매하고 있었지만, 그들은 개별 사업체로서 운영되는 경향이 있었다.
explain: 분절 시대 특성 → individual(개별적인).

vocab_choice.en_template: The growth of tour operators began to change the nature of the industry from individual to more {{1:integrated/fragmented}} activities.
vocab_choice.ko_full: 투어 오퍼레이터의 성장은 산업의 성격을 개별적인 것에서 보다 통합된 활동으로 바꾸기 시작했다.
explain: 변화의 방향은 분절(fragmented)에서 '통합(integrated)'으로.

vocab_choice.en_template: Hotels were beginning to see customers as wanting {{1:a range of/a single}} services rather than simply buying {{2:accommodation/insurance}}.
vocab_choice.ko_full: 호텔들은 단순히 숙박을 구매하는 것보다 오히려 다양한 서비스를 원하는 고객들을 바라보기 시작했다.

이전에 판매하던 단일 상품은 숙박 → accommodation.

vocab_choice.en_template: Hotels began to develop shopping arcades and offer secretarial centres to try to {{1:increase/decrease}} the {{2:spend/revenue}} of guests within the hotel complex.

'투숙객의 지출(액)' → spend(명사).

vocab_choice.en_template: Transport operators saw the sale of transport services as being {{1:integral/irrelevant}} to a much {{2:wider/narrower}} need.
vocab_choice.ko_full: 운송 업체들은 교통 서비스의 판매가 훨씬 더 광범위한 필요와 불가분의 관계에 있다고 보았다.

explain: 항공사가 제공한 첫 번째 확장 서비스 → insurance(보험).

변화 이후 상태 → integrated(통합된).

jumble.answer: Before the 1950s, tourism was very much an industry which was fragmented; hotels, transport operators, travel agents, and tour operators all tended to work independently of each other.
Hotels were largely in the business of selling bed nights.
Airlines and railways were in the business of selling seats.
Travel agents, of course, were selling travel and holidays, but in each case they tended to operate very much as individual businesses.

From the mid-1950s onwards, particularly in the UK, the growth of tour operators began to change the nature of the industry from essentially individual business activities to more integrated activities.
Hotels, for example, were beginning to see customers as wanting a range of services rather than simply buying accommodation.
So hotels began to develop shopping arcades and later to offer secretarial centres to try to increase the spend of guests within the hotel complex.
Transport operators, particularly in the airline business, saw the sale of transport services as being integral to a much wider need.
Airlines offered insurance and accommodation booking for travellers.
So the tourism industry moved from being essentially fragmented to being essentially integrated.
